venue.name: Shawnigan Lake Museum
venue.description: The Shawnigan Lake Museum is operated by the Shawnigan Lake Historical Society, a not for profit registered charity incorporated in 1977, and has run in the village's former firehall since 1983. Its displays cover the Kinsol Trestle, the painter E.J. Hughes, the Canadian Last Spike and other local history, and the society has recently completed an expansion project that tripled the size of the museum. The museum calls itself the unofficial tourist information centre of the South Cowichan Valley and says its docents give every visitor a personal tour. It offers school programming that follows the Big Ideas and Content Expectations of the revised BC curriculum, along with public events and workshops for all ages.
venue.address: 1775 Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay Rd, Shawnigan Lake, BC V8H 3B7

programs.name: School program
programs.description: The museum's school programs page lists options by level. For primary classes it lists Day in the Life of a Pioneer Family, First Peoples and Storywalks. For intermediate classes it lists Kinsol Trestle, First Peoples, Transportation and Industry and Storywalks. The page says the programming follows the Big Ideas and Content Expectations from the revised BC Curriculum and invites teachers to ask about other options. It gives no prices, no group sizes, no lengths and no grade ranges, and booking is by emailing the museum. For parking, the museum asks visitors to use the lot just below the museum, Shawnigan-Mill Bay Rd, Shawnigan Lake Road, or the Community Centre parking lot.
programs.our_note: The site names the programs but publishes nothing about price, length, group size or which grades each one suits, so plan on one email to settle all of it. The teacher comments they quote come from a Grade 1 class and a Grade 6/7 class, which is a fair sign of the range they handle. Parking is street and lot parking in the village, and nothing on the site says where a bus would go.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms, indoor lunch space, step free access and a wet weather plan are not mentioned anywhere on the site, so ask about all of them when you book. The museum is a small former firehall in the village and there is nothing published about bus parking.
programs.evidence: The Shawnigan Lake Museum is proud to offer school programming that follows the Big Ideas and Content Expectations from the revised BC Curriculum.

images.alt: A steam train with passenger carriages stands on a track beside a lake, with a large crowd of people on the grass by a two storey white wooden building and forest behind.
Four children stand around a wooden display case in a museum room while an adult holds up a framed picture, with a wall screen and wooden cabinets behind.
A dark red timber building with a shingled roof and a covered entrance stands beside a paved road, with a vertical MUSEUM sign, yellow bollards and conifers behind.

gaps: No admission price is published for the museum, and no price is published for the school program.
The school programs page gives no grade or age range beyond the words primary and intermediate, no length, no group size limit and no notice period.
months unknown: the school programs page does not say what time of year the programs run, or which days of the week.

Nothing is published about washrooms, an indoor lunch space, a wet weather plan, step free or stroller access, or bus parking. The homepage lists four places to park cars but says nothing about buses.
Opening hours differ between their own pages, so hours are left blank here and the disagreement is recorded as a conflict.

The street name is written as Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay Rd on most pages and Shawnigan-Mill Bay Rd on the press kit and homepage. The postal code V8H 3B7 comes from the mailing address block, which is the same building.
No coordinates are published on the site, so the address is recorded for geocoding in a later pass.
The Open Graph image is the museum's Meet me at the Museum wordmark rather than a photograph, so it was not used as the hero image.

The site writes a file name into the alt attribute of every photograph on it, which is an accessibility failure a screen reader will read out loud. The alt text on all three photographs recorded here was written by us after opening each image in a browser and looking at it, and is marked as generated.

THIS PASS (2026-09-07): opened the two photographs already in this record in a browser and replaced their file name alt text with written descriptions of what is actually in the frame. Took the larger versions of both images that the site also serves. Added the photograph of the museum building from the outside, which is the most useful one on the site for a group arriving.
The museum says its docents give every visitor a personal tour, but there is no page, price or booking route published for a general group visit as distinct from a school booking.
The site is silent on whether it takes daycare or preschool groups, and no minimum age is published.

conflicts.note: Their own pages give two different opening times. Most of the site says they open at 10:00 and their press kit page says 9:30. Both agree on Tuesday to Saturday, closing at 3:30. Worth settling when you book.
